mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 3% over a 3-month window signals a tightening monetary regime, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS > 3.0% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during episodes where GDPC1 YoY change < -2%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE > 6.0% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which depresses earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during four consecutive months of INDPRO declines.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a fall in payroll employment (PAYEMS) by more than 1% month-over-month jointly signal a sharp labor market deterioration, which reduces consumer demand and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls by >1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls by >1% MoM.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for three consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month MA by >10% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during three consecutive months where HOUST exceeds its 12-month MA by >10%.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated fall in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in the same month signals a deflationary easing cycle, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both fall by >0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL fall by >0.5% in the same month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average by more than 5% for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, which typically foreshadows a future consumption rebound and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month MA by >5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during four consecutive months where RSAFS exceeds its 12-month MA by >5%.
